target_customer: Sales and marketing teams, from small businesses to enterprises, that need B2B contact data and outreach tools
problem: Sales teams struggled to find accurate prospect contacts and run outreach without expensive enterprise data tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscriptions with a freemium tier, per seat and credits

founders.name: Tim Zheng
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO with no bio.

founders.name: Ray Li
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder. Seedtable via search also names Roy Chung; not on the YC page and not recorded.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building and keeping a large B2B contact database fresh plus an outreach engine is standard engineering with data pipeline challenges.

defensibility.rationale: Aggregated contact data and workflow lock in help, but data vendors and outreach tools can copy features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not buy it; Apollo grew independently and was valued at 1.6 billion dollars in 2023 per a TechCrunch headline on its YC page.

market_need_then: Sales teams paid heavily for contact data and prospecting tools and wanted cheaper options, though no 2016 spend figures were read.

branding.name_origin: Search coverage says Apollo.io was chosen in 2018 to evoke the Apollo space program moonshot; the earlier name was ZenProspect.
branding.domain_note: Uses apollo.io rather than an exact .com; no purchase detail found.

identity.logo: A later visual rebrand refreshed the logo and color palette per a Paddle write-up seen via search

branding.brand_signature: Moonshot positioning of the Apollo name

rebrands.why: Sources say the product outgrew its first name and similar names caused confusion; from aggregator pages

branding.community_and_virality: No sourced evidence of merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Apollo.io became widely known in sales software with G2 category rankings, but common name causes confusion with other Apollo companies and no source credits the name for growth.

pivots.to: Apollo.io sales intelligence and engagement platform
pivots.why: Rebrand and product expansion reported by aggregator sources; details unverified

outcome_analysis: Apollo.io grew from a YC W16 startup into a unicorn with a 1.6 billion dollar valuation in a 100 million dollar 2023 round, after 32 million in 2021 and 110 million in 2022. A freemium data and engagement product competing with ZoomInfo appears to have driven adoption. It remains private, bought Pocus in March 2026 per search results, and has no reported layoffs or IPO.
notes: The company website fetch was rate limited and the YourStory page returned 403 on fetch; the Series C is cited from the YC page headline (TechCrunch, March 2022) and a search snippet of YourStory. The Series D is labelled other because sources use the label Series D in aggregators but I did not open the primary article. Seed (about 2.2 million, 2016) and Series A (about 7 million, 2018) appear only in aggregators with conflicting dates, so they are unverified. Total raised conflicts between 151 and 273 million, so gaps exist. No dated 2016 competitor source was found.
